solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Realistic ends for partner — to play single guy

indicators.note: the ends of the word partner are its first and last letters only

parts.note: to play a part on stage is to act
single means one, the Roman numeral I
a guy is a rope or cable that steadies a mast or tent

explanation.surface: A dating plan where a lone man pretends to be someone's partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' looks like a man, but here it is a guy rope, a cable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something practicable can actually be done, so it is a realistic option.

clue.text: Practise without ultimate sweetheart then tries again

indicators.note: without the ultimate tells us to drop a letter from the very end of the word

parts.note: to practise for a performance is to rehearse
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: Someone rehearses a romantic scene without their lover and keeps trying again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' is the heart of 'sweet', E; taking the final E off REHEARSE leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A court that rehears a case tries it again, hearing the matter a second time.

clue.text: Pinch criminals before the audience's swindled

parts.note: cons is short for convicts, criminals in prison

indicators.note: what an audience hears is the spoken sound, so this word is given as pronounced

parts.note: swindled means tricked

explanation.surface: Criminals con a theatre audience before the show.
explanation.walkthrough: TRICT is not a word: it just sounds like 'tricked'.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrict is to squeeze or narrow, much as to pinch is to squeeze tightly.

clue.text: Oddly indulged by day and did nothing

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters of the word indulged, first, third, fifth and seventh

explanation.surface: Someone indulged all day and achieved nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To idle is to laze about without working, so idled means stayed inactive.

clue.text: Copper's caught by top defender's first defendant

indicators.note: caught by means held inside another piece, so the copper part is enclosed

parts.note: ace means top or first-rate, as in an ace player
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, plus the S of the possessive

indicators.note: first here takes the opening letter of the word defender's

explanation.surface: A policeman is tackled by the star defender at football.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal, chemical symbol Cu.
explanation.definitionFit: The person charged in court, the defendant, is known as the accused.

clue.text: Left posh medic with earlier complaint

parts.note: U is the old British label for upper-class, posh usage
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
earlier means ago, as in years ago

explanation.surface: A patient leaves a smart doctor having complained earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbago is pain in the lower back, an ailment or bodily complaint.

clue.text: Doctor in Caesareans sidestepping an advanced new birth

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with or alter it, so the letters are rearranged
sidestepping means avoiding, so one letter is left out of the word Caesareans

parts.note: A stands for advanced, as in the British A level

explanation.surface: A doctor performs caesarean births while avoiding an advanced case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the obstetrician but signals the anagram; 'an' is just a link. Removing one A from CAESAREANS and adding IN gives the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Renaissance literally means rebirth, from French, so a new birth.

clue.text: It's right for page to lead Queen

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: A royal page leads the Queen in a procession, as is proper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lead' just puts PRO and P ahead of ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper and right are synonyms: both mean correct or fitting.

clue.text: From rear, the nude's made of clay

indicators.note: from means the letters are drawn out of the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: A sculpture of a nude seen from behind, modelled in clay.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthen pottery is made of fired clay or earth.

clue.text: Doctors left other cases using medical skills initially

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Doctors deal with the remaining cases using medical know-how.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like 'remaining' but is just L.
explanation.definitionFit: Locums are doctors who stand in temporarily for another practitioner.

clue.text: Shout over delay over one's point for set

parts.note: to shout is to cry out
to stall is to delay
one is I, plus the S of the possessive
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Someone shouts again and again about a delay over a point.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places each piece above the next.
explanation.definitionFit: When a liquid sets into solid form it can crystallise, hardening into crystals.

clue.text: When parking, stop to find cover on street

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left
P is the sign and abbreviation for parking
to halt is to stop

explanation.surface: A motorist pulls over to park and find shelter on the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphalt is the tarry surfacing laid over a road, covering the street.

clue.text: Hit rock bottom and aspired to change

indicators.note: to change means the letters of aspired are reordered

explanation.surface: A climber with high aspirations hit rock bottom and had to change.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose all hope is to despair, feeling as low as one can get.

clue.text: Types one letter for 'Saint' or two reversed?

parts.note: S is the one-letter abbreviation for Saint

indicators.note: reversed means the two-letter form is read backwards

parts.note: two letters for Saint gives ST, the usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: A question about how to abbreviate Saint, with one letter or two backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorts and types are synonyms for kinds or classes.

clue.text: Devious, doing time, endless debts to pay

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a prisoner doing time is inside
IOUs are written promises of debts to be paid

explanation.surface: A crook in prison with endless debts behaves deviously.
explanation.definitionFit: Insidious means sly and treacherous, working harm by stealth, which is devious.

clue.text: Coin is up in the air after small doubt

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing

indicators.note: things up in the air are unsettled, so these letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: A coin is tossed after a small doubt arises.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspicion is a feeling of doubt or mistrust about something.

clue.text: Airborne soldier in suitable American machine

indicators.note: in means the soldier is placed inside the other word

parts.note: apt means suitable
a para is a paratrooper, an airborne soldier

explanation.surface: A paratrooper climbs into a suitable American machine.
explanation.definitionFit: An apparatus is a piece of equipment or machinery for a task.

clue.text: Top of pie put on last dish

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the latter is the last of two

explanation.surface: Put the pie crust on last and serve on a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A platter is a large flat plate, a serving dish.

clue.text: Set off again in leisure craft

parts.note: rest is time at leisure
art is skill or craft

explanation.surface: Sailors set off again in a pleasure boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leisure craft' looks like a boat but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To restart is to start again, setting off once more.

clue.text: Described by 'Assassin in Japan'?

definitions.note: the whole clue is a description: the trained killers of feudal Japan

indicators.note: described by means contained within the words that follow, which hold the answer in their letters

explanation.surface: A question about how a Japanese killer might be described.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the end of 'Assassin', all of 'in' and the start of 'Japan'; the whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninjas were covert agents and killers in feudal Japan, skilled in espionage.

clue.text: Sense I'm out to get vengeance

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone senses they are out to get revenge.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis was the Greek goddess of retribution, so the word means downfall or vengeance.

clue.text: Scandinavian Odin with calmer exterior, curiously

indicators.note: curiously means in an odd way, so the letters are mixed
the exterior of a word is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Odin, the Norse god, seems curiously calm on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: The outer letters of 'calmer' are CR; with ODIN they rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Nordic describes the peoples and countries of Scandinavia.

clue.text: Cold young woman, almost glacial model

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a lass is a young woman

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: glacial means icy

explanation.surface: An aloof young woman makes a classically cool fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' looks like the young woman's job but is the definition, as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic example is a model one, the standard against which others are judged.

clue.text: 'Clash' group's approaching start of gig

parts.note: a clan is a family group

indicators.note: start of takes the first letter of the word gig

explanation.surface: The Clash, a punk band, approaching the start of a gig.
explanation.walkthrough: The Clash was a British punk band, but here 'Clash' is a verb: a clang is a metallic crash.
explanation.definitionFit: To clang is to make a loud ringing metallic noise, as clashing cymbals do.

clue.text: Wicked compiler's said to embrace maiden

indicators.note: to embrace means to hold, so one letter is put inside

parts.note: the compiler is the setter, I, so compiler's is I am, written I'M
said means spoken, oral
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: The setter says they are hugging a young woman, which is wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maiden' looks like a girl but is M, a maiden over in cricket, one with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: Immoral and wicked both describe behaviour that breaks moral principles.

clue.text: A pastry's rolled in layers

indicators.note: rolled means turned over, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: a tart is a pastry, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A pastry is rolled out in layers.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata are layers, as of rock or of society.

clue.text: Drills hip and cuts back

parts.note: hip and in both mean fashionable

indicators.note: back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: slits are cuts

explanation.surface: A carpenter drills a joint and cuts the timber back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drills' looks like a tool but is the verb, to teach by repetition.
explanation.definitionFit: To instil an idea is to drill it into someone gradually.

clue.text: Star of 'Argo' isn't top unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: The lead actor of the film Argo didn't come out on top.
explanation.definitionFit: The protagonist is the main character in a story, its star.
